rationale: Execute the accepted current-campaign support question through real producers and independent message-term accounting.

question.question: After a candidate starts a second real campaign, can delayed genuine grant responses from its first campaign contribute to leadership before a majority of current-term grants has been delivered?
question.importance: Counting old-term grants as support for a new campaign would break local authority qualification. The direct question is current-term election support, not a demonstrated conflicting leader or client decision.
participants: FIFO local storage workers and transport scheduler
objects: Actual first and second campaign vote requests/responses
contexts: Three fixed bootstrapped voters, AsyncStorageWrites, PreVote disabled
Two explicit Campaign calls before any first-campaign grant is delivered to the candidate
First and second campaign responses retain original message identity and term
event_paths: Campaign term 2 -> actual peer grants/self grant packaged after storage; transport holds responses
Campaign term 3 -> reset votes and emit actual new requests; independently hold new grants
Release actual term-2 grants, then current self grant and one remote term-3 grant; observe BasicStatus after each fixed phase

supporting_behavior_ids.B_step_context_and_storage: Filters stale terms before candidate response tally.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_append_response_packaging: Publishes real and self vote responses only after local storage work.

counterevidence: Step returns on lower-term ordinary responses, so old VoteResp should never reach poll.
becomeCandidate resets Votes and increments term.
stepCandidate independently rejects pre-vote response type during real candidacy.
question.trigger_rationale: The sender map carries no term tag, so freshness depends on the preceding gate and reset. Consecutive campaigns with delayed genuine responses test this concrete dependency; current self-plus-peer grants supply a permitted control. This avoids the unresolved snapshot/configuration caller contract.

candidate.rationale: Fix local current-term majority eligibility from vote-result and term-dispatch contracts, retaining pending phases as permitted.

obligation.description: An ordinary candidate must not acquire leadership in its current campaign by counting delayed lower-term vote grants; a majority of delivered grants for the current campaign term is necessary.

scope.description: Two consecutive real campaigns by node 1 in a fixed three-voter async cluster; all genuine first- and second-term grants are stored then delayed by transport and released in six fixed phases.
assumptions: PreVote disabled; no timers, configuration changes, snapshots, restarts or external term inputs during the measured suffix.
Sequential RawNode calls, reliable FIFO local append/apply workers; only network vote response delivery is delayed.
MemoryStorage models the stable vote completion boundary in a no-crash schedule.
excluded: General consensus correctness, split-brain history, client effects and physical crash durability.
Pre-vote, joint membership and arbitrary concurrent competing candidates.
A liveness guarantee that sufficient grants must produce leadership by a deadline.

grounding.derivation: VoteResult defines winning as a voter majority of yes votes; stepCandidate consumes that result to acquire leadership. Step dispatch associates ordinary replies with the current term and discards lower-term replies, while real candidacy increments term and resets vote bookkeeping. send documents persistence before vote publication. The scoped necessary condition is that leadership in the second campaign requires a delivered grant majority from that campaign term. A first-term persisted grant is not current-term support merely because its sender remains a voter.
grounding.applicability: Local election-support qualification for three fixed voters and ordinary real campaigns; this code-grounded duty does not by itself establish a conflicting leader consequence.
alternatives: A pending candidate with insufficient current support is permitted.
Both remote voters could supply a majority without self response; this selected schedule instead uses current self plus peer 2.

bindings.description: Consumes admitted vote responses and becomes leader only when poll returns VoteWon; Step performs term admission before this function.

associations.rationale: The consumer acquires leadership from the current campaign support set; delayed lower-term replies must not become qualifying support.

feedback.answered: The fixed driver obtains all six grants from actual campaigns and verifies their stored vote at transport capture. Its independent ledger distinguishes original message terms, and its bounded scheduler does not depend on leadership. No exploration or past test outcome is substituted for this formal execution.
remaining: Trusted execution must establish the actual two-campaign prefix, six comparisons and current-grant control.
Current checker correspondence is required after execution.
feedback.rationale: The decisive phases are delivery of all three old grants with zero current grants, then one current grant, then a current majority.
